title: England (Great Britain) 1688-1760: central government expenditure, interest payments, receipts, national debt and long-term interest rates (annual)
source: Bank of England, 'A millennium of macroeconomic data for the UK' (version 3.1): sheet 'A27. Central govt borrowing' (Mitchell 1988, pp. 575-593), sheet 'A29. The National Debt' (Mitchell 1988; capital value of terminable annuities from Parliamentary Papers 1898) and sheet A31 on interest rates (yields as documented there; mortgage rate from Allen 1988)
series: A27, financial years ending at Michaelmas (September), '1693/94' stored as 1693: 'Total expenditure' (expenditure_gbp_m), 'o/w interest payments' (interest_gbp_m), 'Total receipts' (receipts_gbp_m), £ m. A29, par values at the end of the financial year, £ m: 'Funded Debt of Great Britain' (funded_debt_gbp_m), unfunded debt from Mitchell (1988) (unfunded_debt_gbp_m), 'Total funded and unfunded debt of the UK' (total_debt_gbp_m), 'Estimated capital value of terminable annuities' (annuities_value_gbp_m), the spliced total including that value (debt_incl_annuities_gbp_m) and that total as a per cent of nominal GDP (debt_pct_gdp, from 1699). A31: 'Yield on perpetual annuities/consols' (yield_long_pct, from 1703; 1703-1726 yields on new long-term issues, 1727-1753 the yield on 3% perpetual annuities, then Consols; annual average) and the 'Mortgage Interest Rate' (mortgage_rate_pct, Allen 1988)
license: The workbook asks users to cite the underlying sources (here Mitchell 1988 and Allen 1988). The Bank of England publishes it as a research dataset; a subset (73 years, 11 columns) is stored here for teaching, with attribution.
notes: Workbook SHA-256 4c23dd392a498691eac92659aec283fb43f28118bd80511dc87fc595974195eb. The A27 values for 1688-1690 are identical (the workbook spreads one figure over these years), so they are not read as annual changes. Debt is first reported for 1690. Par (nominal) values: a perpetual annuity counts at its nominal capital, and terminable (life and long) annuities are not in the total debt but in the separate estimate of their capital value; the spliced total adds the two. The yields before 1727 are those of new long-term loans, not market yields on outstanding stock, and the 1703-1709 value is one figure repeated. The chapter divides debt by receipts as a debt-to-revenue ratio comparable with Drelichman and Voth's for Castile (snapshot dv2010_philip2); the two series are built differently and the comparison shows orders of magnitude only.
citation: Mitchell, B. R. (1988), British Historical Statistics, Cambridge University Press, pp. 575-593 and the national debt tables; Allen, R. C. (1988), 'The price of freehold land and the interest rate in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries', Economic History Review 41(1): 33-50, doi:10.2307/2597331; data via Bank of England, A Millennium of Macroeconomic Data for the UK, v3.1 (R. Thomas and N. Dimsdale, 2017)
